transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-19 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees (Redwood): Meera Patel (AE), Jamal Ortiz (SE)
- Attendees (Aurum Layer): Lena Kor (Head of Partnerships), Rajesh Nair (CTO), Tina Morales (Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Quick partner orientation between Redwood and Aurum Layer. Primary goals: clarify channel/reseller model, tech integration options (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security/compliance expectations (SOC2, KMS), and scope a short technical POC to validate latency and throughput for Aurum's inference-on-demand use case. Agreed to a technical scoping session and to exchange security artifacts.

Topics (auto sections - may be imperfect):
- Partner program & commercial model
- Integration patterns (API, SDK, private deployment)
- Security — SOC2, encryption, audit logs, SSO
- Pilot/benchmark plan (100k tokens, latency targets)
- Next steps & owners

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Meera (Redwood AE): Hey — good afternoon from SF — thanks for making time. I'll do a quick intro and Jamal will jump into the tech.
[00:00:12] Lena (Aurum): Hi Meera, thanks. We wanted to get a sense of how Redwood thinks about channel partners and where Aurum could fit. We've got reseller relationships and also a managed infra offering for media companies.
[00:00:25] Meera: Awesome — yeah, short version: Redwood has a partner track that includes reseller, referral, and engineering integration. For engineering we often do a 'channel onramp' where we validate network/topology, sample workloads, and then propose a Dedicated pilot or a private deployment depending on security needs.
[00:00:40] Rajesh (Aurum, CTO): Quick clarification — when you say Dedicated, is that a reserved GPU pool in your cloud, or something we can white-label?
[00:00:50] Jamal (Redwood SE): Great question. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in Redwood's infra — customer isolated pools. We offer a dedicated capacity product that can be dedicated to a partner/customer and be white-labeled in the sense of routing and custom logos in console, but the control plane is still Redwood-managed unless you go Private (VPC/on-prem).
[00:01:10] Tina (Aurum): And Private would be fully inside our VPC / on-prem? We have clients demanding single-tenant air-gapped options.
[00:01:18] Jamal: Correct — Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane, optional on-prem package. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and can ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[00:01:30] Lena: Ok makes sense. Can you talk through common constraints you see with partners doing media inference? We do lots of short-sequence transcode and captioning workloads.
[00:01:42] Jamal: Sure — for media captioning, the big levers are: sequence length distribution (short vs batched longer sequences), prefix caching (we support KV cache but some transcripts transcribe it as KV "cash" in older notes), and batching windows. For captioning you want low tail latency, so we often recommend a lower batch timeout and a model variant with faster quantized execution.
[00:02:05] Meera: And from commercial side, partner program has a margin tier and credit for POC runs. We'll send the program one-pager.
[00:02:12] Rajesh: On security — we need SOC2, ISO; also need to know retention windows and where customer data is stored.
[00:02:20] Jamal: We have a SOC2 report and ISO docs — we'll share the security pack. Data for hosted API is stored in our cloud regions; Dedicated also keeps logs per-tenant. We support encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS integration for Private. Audit logs can be exported to your Splunk or S3.
[00:02:38] Tina: Does Redwood support bringing your own key (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys for Private?
[00:02:43] Jamal: Yes — BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported in Private. For Dedicated we use Redwood-managed keys but can negotiate enterprise KMS integrations depending on contract.
[00:02:55] Lena: Cool. On the reseller side, if Aurum resells Redwood services, how does billing flow?
[00:03:02] Meera: Typically we do a partner billing arrangement — we invoice the partner for reserved capacity or usage, partner bills their end customers with negotiated margin. We have marketplace options too. We'll send partner billing docs.
[00:03:15] Rajesh: On networking — some of our clients require egress restrictions, and our infra is VPC peered with multiple clouds. Can you outline the connectivity options?
[00:03:25] Jamal: Sure — options: 1) Public API with IP allowlist, 2) VPC peering/PrivateLink to Redwood region, 3) Full private control plane for Private deployments. For on-prem we can deploy into your kube or as a pre-packaged VM set. Note: our orchestration expects GPUs with certain drivers; we can provide a checklist.
[00:03:45] Tina: Are there known driver or CUDA versions that are mandatory? We run a mix of A100 and H100 in our pools.
[00:03:52] Jamal: H100 is supported — we auto-select kernels — but there are recommended driver+CUDA combos. We'll attach a HW compatibility matrix. Sometimes my notes say "cube-ernet-us" instead of Kubernetes — transcriptions get weird.
[00:04:10] Lena: Ha, we see that.
[00:04:13] Meera: Quick commercial guardrail — if you want a pilot with Dedicated, we'd need a short SOW and a commit for the pool size. There's a light pilot with a time-boxed reserved capacity that's common.
[00:04:25] Rajesh: For a technical pilot, our success criteria would be: p95 latency under 180ms for short captions (avg 30 tokens), and cost per 1k tokens below X — we'd have to share numbers.
[00:04:36] Jamal: That sounds reasonable — we can run a 100k token pilot with high-fidelity CPU/GPU metrics and token-level cost breakdown in the Console. We can also run a stress test to surface SLOs.
[00:04:48] Tina: How do you handle model fallbacks if capacity is constrained? We can't have customers failing during peak events.
[00:04:55] Jamal: We have smart routing — fallback to compatible model variants (slightly cheaper/faster) and region failover. For guaranteed capacity you choose Dedicated or Private. Hosted API has fallback policies but no capacity guarantee.
[00:05:05] Meera: On the partner enablement side, we provide a partner kit: docs, demo decks, postman collections, and a co-marketing budget for qualified partners.
[00:05:12] Lena: Great. Anything special around SSO / RBAC for partner admins?
[00:05:18] Jamal: We integrate with SAML/SSO providers and have RBAC roles for partner admins and customer teams. You can set token-level audit.
[00:05:28] Rajesh: One technical nit — do you support streaming outputs for live captions?
[00:05:33] Jamal: Yes — streaming with chunked responses and partial tokens is supported; we also have function-calling style hooks for structured outputs if you need labelled timestamps. There may be small variance in transcript; sometimes it gets transcribed as function "calling" in the export.
[00:05:48] Meera: Let's move to POC scope — Jamal, could you sketch the test plan?
[00:05:53] Jamal: Sure. Proposed POC: 1) baseline run on Hosted API for 10k tokens to validate correctness and streaming behavior; 2) Dedicated trial with reserved pool for 100k tokens focusing on latency tail (p95/p99); 3) run a concurrency test to simulate 200 simultaneous short requests. We'll collect token-level cost, GPU utilization, and tail latency.
[00:06:18] Lena: For the baseline, would that be on a specific open model? We test on a few LLMs for captioning.
[00:06:24] Jamal: We can recommend variants — for captioning maybe a trimmed causal model or a quantized variant. We'll propose two model candidates. We'll also include a note about quantization tradeoffs — lower cost but small quality delta.
[00:06:38] Rajesh: How quickly can you spin up a Dedicated pool for a pilot?
[00:06:42] Meera: Depends on size and contract — small dedicated pools can be provisioned in days to a week. If it's private/on-prem, that's longer. We'll coordinate with provisioning.
[00:06:52] Tina: Ok, operational: what observability do you expose? We need per-route latency, token counts, and trace ids.
[00:06:58] Jamal: Console exposes per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, p50/p95/p99, trace ids, and raw logs for the pilot. We can add an agent for pushing metrics to your Datadog.
[00:07:12] [00:07:12] (crosstalk) Rajesh: That would be useful...
[00:07:18] Meera: A couple of compliance questions that pop up often — retention windows: can you auto-delete request logs after X days?
[00:07:24] Jamal: Yes — retention is configurable per-tenant for Dedicated/Private; hosted has defaults but can be discussed in enterprise contracts.
[00:07:34] Lena: Great. On partner marketing: we sometimes co-sell with white-labeled dashboards; does Redwood allow that?
[00:07:41] Meera: We can support co-branded dashboards and there's an MSP track with co-sell incentives.
[00:07:48] Rajesh: Any performance caveats for models when using quantization or KV caching? We've seen artifacts in paraphrase for some models.
[00:07:56] Jamal: Tradeoff: quantization reduces memory and cost but can slightly affect generation quality. KV cache helps for prefix heavy workloads. We recommend a small eval set to determine acceptable quality delta; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions and we can run evals tied to your prompt sets.
[00:08:14] Tina: If we run an on-prem package, does Redwood provide patching and support or is that on us?
[00:08:20] Jamal: For on-prem, there's an enterprise support add-on where Redwood provides updates, monitoring, and a support SLA. If you self-manage, we provide the packages and documented upgrade steps.
[00:08:32] Lena: Sounds good. I'd like to surface two internal asks: 1) a short partner economics example, and 2) a technical checklist for onboarding clients via Aurum.
[00:08:40] Meera: We'll deliver both. Jamal will add the technical checklist.
[00:08:45] Jamal: Yep — items we'll share: HW/drivers matrix, recommended CUDA/driver combos, recommended model variants for captioning, sample benchmark scripts, and a network topology diagram.
[00:08:58] Rajesh: About costs — can you give a rough ballpark of per-token on Hosted vs Dedicated? We just need order-of-magnitude to decide pilot size.
[00:09:06] Meera: I'll send preliminary numbers in the partner one-pager — hosted api typically has a higher per-token list price, Dedicated reduces unit cost with reserved commits. We'll include an example showing unit economics with 100k tokens.
[00:09:18] Tina: Any regulatory compliance notes for EU-based clients? We have customers in EU and data residency is critical.
[00:09:25] Jamal: Redwood has region options and can deploy Dedicated in EU regions. For Private we can deploy inside EU on-prem. SOC2 and ISO docs also apply.
[00:09:34] Lena: Ok, moving toward logistics: propose we run the technical scoping next week — a 2-hour deep-dive with Rajesh + Tina + our infra team and Jamal.
[00:09:44] Meera: That works. How about Wednesday 2026-07-22 in the morning?
[00:09:50] Rajesh: Wednesday morning PST is fine.
[00:09:53] Meera: Cool, I'll send the invite and the pre-read (security pack + partner one-pager).
[00:09:59] [00:09:59] (brief silence)
[00:10:05] Jamal: Quick aside — we've seen some partners run into a live captioning edge-case where low-latency constraints forced them to avoid batching entirely; in those cases we tune the runtime to favor single-request throughput and prioritize KV caching on the CPU path. Notes sometimes said "KV cash" or "KV cacheors" in older notes.
[00:10:23] Lena: Ha — noted.
[00:10:26] Meera: OK we'll wrap with concrete next steps.
[00:10:30] Meera: Next steps recap: 1) Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 (Meera) — due 2026-07-22; 2) Redwood SE to share benchmark runbook and sample scripts (Jamal) — due 2026-07-23; 3) Aurum to share representative workloads and egress constraints (Rajesh) — due 2026-07-24; 4) Schedule 2-hour technical scoping session on 2026-07-22 (Meera to send invite).
[00:10:54] Lena: That captures it. Any blockers from Redwood?
[00:10:58] Meera: No blockers — just aligning dates and paperwork for the pilot.
[00:11:02] Rajesh: One last question — do you have a partner sandbox account with pre-provisioned tokens for testing?
[00:11:07] Meera: Yes we can provision a sandbox with limited quota for Aurum. We'll include instructions in the partner kit.
[00:11:15] Tina: Great, thanks all.
[00:11:17] Meera: Thanks everyone — look forward to next week.
[00:11:20] Lena: Thanks.
